details:
Currently the COPY instruction will automatically change the IStrongBox internal type for a heap variable if you attempt to assign a type that does not match exactly. This works well for a language that's weakly typed, but for strongly typed languages like C# this has a few problems that can break conventions in weird ways for the user.
What this means in effect is that there is no explicit casting between types in UdonVM as-is. We cannot tell it to turn a specific type into another. This has a few issues and limitations that come with it. So it would be nice to have an UdonVM instruction that force assigns a value to a heap strongbox value without changing the strongbox type and throws a runtime exception on failure to assign the type. 


Here's a few specific limitations we've run into so far:
a. System.Convert works a majority of the time for numeric conversions, but there are cases where it doesn’t behave the same as the dedicated CIL cast instructions. For instance, System.Convert does not support directly converting `char` to `float` whereas `Debug.Log((float)’a’)` is perfectly valid C# since the CIL instructions handle the cast properly. https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-bugs/p/convert-to-float-exception-when-converting-char-to-float 
b. You can cast integers to enums in C# `(HumanBodyBones)18` will give the enum value for HumanBodyBones.RightHand for instance. This is commonly used to iterate over all values of an enum. In Udon without special functions to emulate this behaviour https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/provide-enum-constructor-that-takes-an-integer-and-converts-it-to-an-enum-of-the , I don’t believe it’s currently possible to cast from int to enum. 
c. The biggest issue IMO is that there is no decent way to check that a class is a subclass of a specific type. It’s currently totally valid to copy a Vector3 into a heap variable that’s declared as a Renderer. Any code that references that heap value from that point on will treat it as a Vector3 and if any functions expect it to be a Renderer, they will break when they try to treat it as a Renderer. This can happen far down the execution chain from where the variable is set and can become more difficult to debug as a result. This can be emulated on the compiler’s side if we had access to more of the System.Type methods https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/expose-systemtypeissubclassof-isinstanceoftype-issubclassof-and-basetype but it would still be more performant to be able to tell the VM to do the cast and checking on its side. Exposing more of System.Type would still be useful for non-throwing type checking like the `is` and `as` operators https://vrchat.canny.io/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/is-operator-with-possible-type-cast , but having a dedicated instruction that throws an exception on invalid cast would be nice for non-value types at least. 
For the class cast checks it should be enough to implement a generic function on the `StrongBox<T>` that takes an object and does `Value = (T)object;` on it. 
For the value type casts, it may require more complex handling since while the CIL instructions are somewhat generalized, I’m not sure how involved complex it would be to use C# primitives for generic casts. The best handling might just be to generate methods that actually do the casts from type to type based on what the CIL instructions for casting allow. In that case it’d be reasonable for me to add handling for those casts. For enum casts, I’ve just seen the CIL copy the int value straight into the enum variable. I don’t know if there’s a way to do that with just C#. Maybe the above linked suggestion of cast constructors for int to enum<T> would be the best. 
I’m not sure what the best course of action on implementing an instruction like this for value types would be, but it would be nice to have for reference types at the very least.
title: Provide an instruction that does not automatically reassign the strongbox type when source and target types differ
